extracted.intended_audience: comedians, comedy writers, and researchers/students studying humor
extracted.subtask_description: Apply cognitive reframing as a joke mechanism: craft a setup and punchline where the punchline forces the audience to reinterpret the setup in a new, surprising frame that is illuminating or truthful. Useful for comedy writers and researchers analyzing joke structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of reframing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reframing means to change the meaning of something by putting it in a different setting, context, or frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core mechanism: change the interpretive frame to change meaning. This is the basic transformational move that produces reinterpretation in the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punchline imposes a new frame on setup material
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the punch impose a new frame on setup material?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly states 'Punchline = forced reframing of setup material.' For production/evaluation, check whether the punch forces a reinterpretation of elements introduced by the setup rather than introducing unrelated material.

rubrics_metrics.name: New frame is illuminating (not arbitrary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the new frame illuminating (not arbitrary)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good reframing should explain, highlight, or make visible something meaningful about the setup; avoid random or purely shock-based reframes that don't add insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes emotional valence
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it change the emotional valence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reframing often shifts the audience's emotional response (e.g., from discomfort to amusement). Evaluate whether the frame change meaningfully alters emotional tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reframing reveals a truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the reframing reveal a truth?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective reframes often expose an underlying truth or observation about behavior, society, or human nature; assess whether the punchline yields an observation that resonates as 'true.'

rubrics_metrics.name: New frame is recognizably new / surprising
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the new frame recognizably new (surprising)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funny = the new frame is unexpected and illuminating. Surprise is a key ingredient—ensure the reinterpretation is not predictable from the setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reinterpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience reinterprets what they just heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reframing relies on the audience mentally revising their prior interpretation. When evaluating, check whether listeners are likely to retroactively reinterpret elements of the setup in light of the punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpectedness / surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: The new frame should be unexpected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely related to 'recognizably new'—this criterion emphasizes that the humor depends on a violation of expectation; consider whether the punchline subverts an expected frame in a way that creates cognitive shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Reframing (same situation, new meaning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Same situation, new meaning. Example: 'I'm not lazy, I'm energy-efficient.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: reinterpret the literal content to a different evaluative meaning. Useful for pithy one-liners that flip an attribute into a virtue or vice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context Reframing (behavior judged differently across contexts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavior is bad in context A, good in context B. Example: 'Stubborn at home; persistent at work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: shift the context to change moral/valuative reading. Works well for contrasts and parallelism between settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Reframing (past distress to present comedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reframe past distress or tragedy as present comedy. Summarized by 'Comedy is tragedy plus time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: distance via time allows painful events to be reframed as amusing; often used in storytelling and observational comedy. Consider ethical/tone constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale Reframing (make small things big or big things small)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make small things big or big things small (hyperbole and understatement as reframings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: alter perceived magnitude to produce contrast. Use hyperbole/understatement deliberately to shift audience valuation of an event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity Reframing (relabeling self/others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinterpret identity or label to change meaning. Example: 'I'm not a hoarder, I'm a curator.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: swap derogatory or mundane labels for more flattering or ironic ones. Effective for character-based jokes and self-deprecation turned into authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor as cognitive/therapeutic tool (positive reframing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor based on positivity is a variant of reframing: shifts perspective of unfavorable event toward a more positive outlook; has therapeutic function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing or evaluating, consider whether reframing moves the audience toward constructive or cathartic appraisal. Also consider limits—positive reframing can downplay harm if used inappropriately.
